Done. I've implemented a full replication of the paper's core experiments, scoped to Gemma and Gemini, plus a `DESIGN.md` documenting every choice. Nothing was run — code and design only, as requested.

## What I built

I read the paper carefully — including the full appendices in `PAPER.txt` (the markdown had them stripped), which gave me the verbatim judge prompts, puzzle specs, training hyperparameters, Petri prompts, and DPO pair examples.

**The two headline deliverables (paper's abstract):**
- **§2 Emotion-elicitation eval suite** — the 8 conditions / 5 categories, multi-turn rejection rollout engine, and the verbatim Claude-Sonnet-4 0–10 frustration judge. Produces the Figure 1 table, Figure 2 (per-category), and Figure 3 (per-turn progression) for `gemma-3-27b-it`, `gemma-3-12b-it`, `gemini-2.5-flash`, `gemini-2.5-pro`.
- **§4 DPO mitigation** — calm-data generation with the reassuring prompt additions, 280-pair construction, TRL+PEFT LoRA DPO/SFT trainers at the exact Table-9 hyperparameters, then re-evaluation through the same suite.

**Supporting experiments:** §3 base-vs-instruct prefill (Gemma only — see below), judge validation (Pearson r vs GPT-5-mini), differential-word analysis (Table 3/8), a self-contained Petri auditor/judge loop, and a capability-preservation regression check.

**Backends:** vLLM for local Gemma (incl. base-model prefill and LoRA serving), OpenRouter for Gemini, Anthropic SDK for judge/auditor — behind one `ChatModel` interface.

## Key judgment calls (all in DESIGN.md)

- **Scope:** §3's cross-family claim needs Qwen/OLMo and Gemini has no public base model, so I reduced §3 to Gemma base-vs-instruct (the in-scope half of the claim) and flagged the rest.
- **8 conditions / 5 categories:** the paper never enumerates the 8; I derived the unique split that matches both the count and every per-category subtotal (opinion+factual triggers; 3 tone styles).
- **Puzzle impossibility:** I wrote verifiers for Countdown/Fraction/Money and ship only machine-verified-impossible instances — stronger than the paper's assertion.
- **Scoring units, DPO pairing anchor, token-truncation proxy, WildChat sampling, max_tokens** — each underspecified point is resolved and justified.

A couple of things I deliberately left as documented gaps rather than half-implementing: the logit-based internal-emotion probe (Appendix I's second method — needs the Gemma unembedding + Ekman lexicon) and the recovery experiment (trivial to add on the existing prefill code). Both are called out explicitly in DESIGN.md §5 so they're not mistaken for oversights.

Note: there's no Python in this environment, so I couldn't byte-compile — I reviewed the code by eye and fixed one real issue along the way (PEFT layer-restriction needs `layers_to_transform`, not regex module names).

Want me to add the recovery experiment and the internal-emotion probe, or run a `--quick` smoke test once you've set up keys/GPUs?
